title: Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) Specialist (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
4. MOS 7051, Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) Specialist (MGySgt to
Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) is highly
specialized. It demands familiarity with aircrew extrication and aircraft
firefighting procedures and techniques for any potential aircraft mishap.
Actions taken by rescuers must be precise and timely. Individuals seeking
assignment to these duties should possess personal qualities that include
alertness, courage, dedication, agility, physical strength, and the ability
to be an exacting team worker. ARFF is a unique capability within the ACE.
ARFF provides aircraft rescue and firefighting services in support of
airfield operations (AirOps) at forward locations and support installations.
The primary and secondary mission of ARFF is to save lives and protect
property. ARFF services include; extrication and/or rescue, fire suppression
and extinguishment, basic emergency medical services, salvage and overhaul
operations, incident command, and immediate hazardous material operations
level response. While supporting Advanced Naval Base and Distributed Aviation
Operation locations, the ARFF platoon is also responsible for the effective
implementation and management of fire protection and prevention programs,
aircraft salvage and recovery operations, Base Recovery After Attack (BRAAT),
and Forward Arming and Refueling Point (FARP).

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Valid state driver's license.

            (3) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

            (4) Must possess a GT score of 90 or MM score of 90 or higher.

        (5) Minimum height requirement to be classified a 7051 is 59 inches
(actual height).

        (6) Vision correctable to 20/20, maximum vision impairment of 20/50
and normal color acuity.

        (7) Must meet the medical standards as required per reference (bc),
The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 1582 and reference (cq), The
Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) 29 Code of Federal
Regulation (CFR) 1910.134.

        (8) Marines interested in requesting a lateral move should contact
their career planner or prior service recruiter to ensure they meet the
prerequisites. Marines meeting the prerequisites will contact the nearest
Senior Enlisted Aircraft and Rescue Fire Fighting Specialist (7051) to begin
the screening process. A letter of recommendation from the Fire and Emergency
Services Officer (7002) and the Senior Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting
Specialist (7051) will be forwarded to the Marines monitor, via the career
planner, to CMC (manpower management enlisted assignments) for final
approval.

        (9) Physical requirements: The duties of the 7051 occupational field
require extended periods of physical exertion while wearing firefighting
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such activities as running, walking,
standing, bending or driving and occasionally lifting, pushing and/or



                                           3-442                        Enclosure (1)
 3146                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



carrying items weighing 50 pounds or more. Requires stamina, physical agility
and dexterity and the strength to save lives or protect property. A 7051
occupational field Marine may be required to push or drag heavy weights of
170 pounds or more and is required to exemplify the physical characteristics
of agility in the performance of their duties.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Fire Protection Apprentice (Air Force) Course
(F0764T2), San Angelo, TX.

        (2) Complete a fire fighter physical prior to attending the Fire
Protection Apprentice Course (F0764T2).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (dq), Expeditionary Firefighting and Rescue (EFR)
Specialist Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Fire Fighters 33-2011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
